title: Methods and data quality
text:
Data sources

Case line list (notification and investigation form): 166 notified cases, from 29 Jan 2026 to 9 Oct 2026.
Contact follow-up database: 387 contacts and 2,917 follow-up visits.
Base maps: 117 health areas and 11 health regions.
Response timeline: MINSAP/INASA, SGI-Mpox.

The data are managed by INASA. This site is regenerated automatically from these sources; the data cut-off is the most recent notification date in the line list.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Definitions

Notified (suspected) case: any person notified under the national case definition, whatever the laboratory result.
Confirmed case: notified case with a positive mpox RT-PCR.
Not confirmed: notified case with a negative RT-PCR (“descartado”).
Pending: notified case whose laboratory result is not yet available or inconclusive.
Epidemiological week: ISO 8601 week, Monday to Sunday (W39 = week 39).
Reference date for curves: date of symptom onset; if missing, date of notification.
Contact under follow-up: contact whose planned end of follow-up (21 days after the last exposure) has not yet been reached, with no closing visit and who has not become a case.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Data protection
No personal data are published on this site: no names, no case or contact identifiers, no addresses, no occupations. Index cases are labelled with a sequence number (“Index case 1”, “Index case 2”…). Individual records are used only for the calculations, on a controlled computer or server, and only aggregated results are published. Figures based on very small numbers (one or two people in a health area) should be interpreted and shared with care.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Data quality







How to read: these indicators flag data to complete or correct in INASA’s database. Outliers are never corrected automatically: they are excluded from the calculation concerned and counted here. Because case identifiers are typed freely (spaces, hyphens, 2- or 4-digit years), contacts are linked to cases through a “region-zone-number” key extracted from the identifier, without approximate matching; a contact whose key matches no case stays unlinked.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Analysis methods

Curves and maps: raw counts by epidemiological week and by health area or region. Population data are not yet integrated, so no incidence rates are calculated.
Positivity rate: confirmed cases / cases tested with a result (pending cases excluded).
Effective reproduction number (Rt): EpiEstim parametric method (Cori et al., 2013) over sliding 14-day windows, from confirmed cases by date of symptom onset; serial interval of 8.5 days (standard deviation 5.0 days), from Miura et al., Emerging Infectious Diseases 2023 (2022 outbreak in the United States). This interval was not measured locally and numbers are small: estimates are indicative.
Symptoms: confirmed vs not confirmed compared with Fisher’s exact test, odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals; combinations computed only on cases with all the signs concerned recorded; sensitivity, specificity and predictive values computed against the RT-PCR result.
Active contacts: contacts for whom the current date falls between the start and the planned end of their 21-day follow-up.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Limitations

The last two weeks are incomplete (reporting and laboratory delays).
The notification form has no field yet on case outcome: deaths are not shown.
Hospitalisation, isolation and epidemiological link are not shown, for lack of reliable information in the forms.
The contact database no longer has an explicit follow-up status: status is derived from visits (“Terminado” visit = follow-up completed; “Tornou-se caso” = became a case; planned end not yet reached = under follow-up; end passed without a closing visit = “not closed”).
Symptom comparisons rest on 29 confirmed cases: confidence intervals are wide.

title: Methods and data quality
text:
Updates
The site is regenerated whenever INASA updates the data: all results are recalculated from the database, with no manual entry. Only the background text on the home page and the timeline are edited by hand.

title: Symptom analysis
text:
Data as of 9 Oct 2026
This page compares the clinical signs of the 29 confirmed cases and the 137 suspected cases that were not confirmed (negative RT-PCR). The 0 cases awaiting a result are excluded. A “no information” answer is never counted as “no”: the case is left out of the calculation for that symptom.

title: Symptom analysis
text:
Frequency of each symptom













How to read: each line joins the frequency of a symptom among non-confirmed cases (blue) and confirmed cases (red). The wider the gap, the better the symptom separates confirmed cases. The odds ratio (OR) measures this association: an OR above 1 means the symptom is more frequent among confirmed cases. With 29 confirmed cases the confidence intervals are wide, and a non-significant difference (p ≥ 0.05) does not show that there is no association.

title: Symptom analysis
text:
Combinations of main signs
Combinations of fever, skin rash and lymphadenopathy, among cases with all three signs recorded.










How to read: each row is a combination of signs (joined black dots); the bar gives the number of cases with that combination, split into confirmed (red) and not confirmed (blue). The share confirmed is shown only from 5 cases upwards. Analysis of 157 cases (9 excluded for missing information on one of the three signs).

title: Symptom analysis
text:
Combinations of lesion types
Stages of skin lesions (macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, crusts) among cases with a rash.










How to read: classically, mpox lesions progress at the same pace, whereas chickenpox lesions appear at different stages at the same time; but during the global clade IIb outbreak of 2022, lesions at different stages were often seen in mpox cases. Lesion stage alone therefore cannot tell the two diseases apart. Analysis of 111 cases with a rash (16 excluded for missing information on one of the lesion types). The 12 most frequent combinations are shown.

title: Symptom analysis
section: How well each sign predicts confirmation
text:
How well each sign predicts confirmation







How to read: sensitivity is the share of confirmed cases that had the sign; specificity, the share of non-confirmed cases that did not. The positive predictive value (PPV) is the probability that a case with the sign is confirmed, in the population tested here: it depends on the positivity rate (17.5%) and does not carry over to another population. These indicators help assess the case definition.

Status of affected health areas







Status is based on the notification date of each area’s last confirmed case: under 21 days, transmission possible; 21 to 42 days, enhanced surveillance; over 42 days, no case for two incubation periods (21 days each). Areas with no confirmed case are listed if they notified a suspected case in the last 21 days. Current count: 4 area(s) where transmission is possible, 5 under enhanced surveillance, 2 with no case for more than 42 days.

title: Mpox outbreak in Guinea-Bissau
text:
Background
The first case of the current mpox outbreak had symptom onset on 13 June 2026 and was laboratory-confirmed on 23 June 2026. The Ministry of Public Health (MINSAP) officially declared the outbreak on 4 July 2026, and sequencing identified clade IIb on 5 July 2026. The response is coordinated by the incident management system (SGI-Mpox), activated on 1 July 2026, with support from the National Institute of Public Health (INASA) and WHO.
The outbreak first affected the Bissau health region (SAB), then Biombo (first confirmed case on 13 July 2026) and Bafatá (14 September 2026). This dashboard presents data from the case line list and the contact follow-up database, and is updated whenever INASA publishes new data.

title: Mpox outbreak in Guinea-Bissau
text:
Situation at a glance

25 cases notified in the last 14 days (26 Sep 2026 to 9 Oct 2026), of which 6 confirmed (−47% compared with the previous two weeks).
Last confirmed case notified on 7 Oct 2026, 2 days ago.
Confirmed cases by region: SAB (Bissau) (23), Bafatá (3), Biombo (3).
17 contacts are still under follow-up; 252 completed the 21-day follow-up and 3 became cases.
On 5 Oct 2026 (latest available window), Rt is estimated at 1.24 (95% CrI: 0.50–2.32), that is above 1 for the central estimate, but the credible interval includes 1: an increase cannot be concluded. Details on the Epidemiological situation page.

title: Epidemiological situation
text:
Effective reproduction number (Rt)







On 5 Oct 2026 (latest available window), Rt is estimated at 1.24 (95% CrI: 0.50–2.32), that is above 1 for the central estimate, but the credible interval includes 1: an increase cannot be concluded. Two weeks earlier (21 Sep 2026), it was 0.76: the recent trend is upward, after reaching 1.78 on 26 Sep 2026. Over the last 4 weeks, the central estimate was above 1 on 64.3% of days, and the whole interval was above 1 on 0.0%. The highest value (5.64, on 11 Jul 2026) dates from a period with few cases, when a small cluster is enough to push the estimate up sharply. Estimates for the last few days are the least reliable: cases with recent symptom onset have not all been reported yet, which pulls Rt down at the end of the period.


Reading Rt: Rt is the average number of people infected by each case at a given date; above 1 (dashed line) the outbreak is growing, below 1 it is declining. It is estimated over sliding 14-day windows from confirmed cases only, by date of symptom onset (EpiEstim parametric method), with a serial interval of 8.5 days on average (standard deviation 5.0 days) taken from the 2022 outbreak in the United States (Miura et al., Emerg Infect Dis 2023), not measured in Guinea-Bissau. With 29 confirmed cases the intervals are wide: the interpretation above is recalculated at each update and only calls a trend clear when the whole interval lies on one side of 1.
